clue.text: Dyke-builder left rubbish

parts.note: Offa, the eighth-century Mercian king, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border

explanation.surface: A builder of earthworks walked off and left a pile of rubbish behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is the great earthwork on the England-Wales border, named for King Offa of Mercia.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is waste matter or refuse, so it serves as a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Title displayed right in the middle of new wineshop

indicators.note: in the middle of tells us one letter is set inside the remaining letters
new signals that the letters of wineshop are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A title is shown right in the centre of a newly opened wine shop's sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns WINESHOP into OWNESHIP, and 'in the middle of' puts R inside it after OWNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Title in the legal sense is the right of possession of property, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Anticipate everyone supporting woodlands?

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: a forest is an extensive area of woodland
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Asks whether everyone backs the protection of woodland areas.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' puts ALL under FOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to prevent something, which is to anticipate it.

clue.text: Fib loudly? Willingly, at one time!

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
F, forte, is the musical direction meaning loudly

explanation.surface: Someone tells a loud fib, and once did so readily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly?' looks like a homophone signal, but it is F, forte in music.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word meant gladly or readily, as in 'I would as lief stay'.

clue.text: To shock, drink quickly

explanation.surface: Taking a swift drink to deal with a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to surprise or upset someone, and also to swallow a drink in one gulp.

clue.text: Disorderly drinkers I'd met in carpet town

indicators.note: Disorderly says the letters of the following words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd of drinkers I came across in a town famous for carpets.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidderminster in Worcestershire, England, is famous for carpet making.
explanation.definitionFit: This Worcestershire town gave its name to a type of carpet woven there for centuries.

clue.text: King can retire to fashion garments by hand

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A monarch can step back from duties to make clothes by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting is making garments from yarn with needles, by hand.

clue.text: To pass, in a university, takes so long

indicators.note: in places the word for passing away inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
to pass away, or simply pass, is to die

explanation.surface: Getting a pass at university takes a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pass' looks like an exam success, but it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells: a French goodbye used in English for parting.

clue.text: Section of broken door used for Japanese fencing

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of a smashed door serves as equipment for Japanese swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Often room for improvement where one works

definitions.text: Often room for improvement where one works

parts.words: Often room for improvement where one works
parts.note: the hospital ward where this carer works is where patients improve, read as a place of work

explanation.surface: A remark that most workplaces leave room for improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for improvement' is a stock phrase for shortcomings; here it is a literal sickroom where patients get better.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer on a hospital ward works in a room where the sick recover.

clue.text: Fare consultant?

parts.note: fare read as food rather than a ticket price, so an adviser on what one eats

explanation.surface: Someone who advises on ticket prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests transport costs, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert advises people on their diet, that is, on food.

clue.text: Iron in coil is currently attractive

definitions.text: Iron in coil is currently attractive

parts.words: Iron in coil is currently attractive
parts.note: a soft iron core in a wire coil pulls metal while electric current flows through it

explanation.surface: Iron in a coil is in fashion right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' seems to mean 'at present' but means 'when current flows'.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is an iron core wound with wire that becomes magnetic when current passes.

clue.text: Unguarded skin trouble

explanation.surface: A careless moment leads to a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means reckless or hasty; as a noun it is an eruption of spots on the skin.

clue.text: Get flat either way

indicators.note: either way says the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Instruction to make something flat however you go about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To level something is to make it flat and even.

clue.text: Dicey way for men on board to get home?

definitions.text: Dicey way for men on board to get home?

parts.words: Dicey way for men on board to get home?
parts.note: dice decide how counters move round a board game toward their home square

explanation.surface: A risky route home for sailors aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicey' sounds like 'risky' and 'men on board' like sailors; it is dice and pieces on a game board.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's board game moves counters by dice throws until they reach home.

clue.text: Number three brought out

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are drawn out and rearranged

explanation.surface: The figure three is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs: the anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This old anaesthetic numbs a patient, so it is a numb-er.

clue.text: Performer who has hard lines sometimes

definitions.text: Performer who has hard lines sometimes

parts.words: Performer who has hard lines sometimes
parts.note: hard lines read as a difficult script to learn, not bad luck

explanation.surface: A performer who sometimes suffers bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines' is British slang for bad luck; here it is a tricky script.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage player learns a script, so sometimes has difficult words to deliver.

clue.text: Opening for people who are not pushy

definitions.text: Opening for people who are not pushy

parts.words: Opening for people who are not pushy
parts.note: an entrance that swings by itself, so nobody needs to push it

explanation.surface: A job opening for the unassertive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a job vacancy and 'pushy' assertiveness; it is a literal entrance needing no push.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor-driven entrance opens itself, so users need not push it.

clue.text: International events in which daily mops out?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Games in which the daily mops are thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympic Games and similar contests between nations are such international competitions.

clue.text: Origin of specie?

parts.note: specie is coin money, so its origin is the place coins are struck; echoes Darwin's book title

explanation.surface: A nod to Darwin's book on the origin of species.
explanation.walkthrough: Specie means coins, not species; the Royal Mint makes Britain's coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state coin factory is where minted money comes from.

clue.text: No late apology, perhaps, for work with old fossils

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A missing apology for lateness, perhaps, for working on old fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: This science studies prehistoric life through fossil remains.

clue.text: Bet with Irish money

explanation.surface: A wager placed with currency from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to gamble; as a noun it was the Irish pound before the euro.

clue.text: But not a girl's best friend, it turns out

definitions.text: But not a girl's best friend, it turns out

parts.words: But not a girl's best friend, it turns out
parts.note: diamonds are said to be a girl's best friend; this glass imitation only looks like one

explanation.surface: Someone turns out not to be a girl's closest friend after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The song says diamonds are a girl's best friend; fake jewels made of glass are not.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is glass used to make imitation gems, a sham diamond.

clue.text: This bottle never runs out!

indicators.note: runs out suggests the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: This bottle is one that is never empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang is courage, which is the same as nerve.

clue.text: Rob's least trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are stirred up into disorder

explanation.surface: Rob has very few problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to take without permission, a synonym of thieving.

clue.text: Middle Wallop always produces such a gem

indicators.note: Middle points to letters taken from the inside of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The village of Middle Wallop always yields this kind of jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle Wallop is a village in Hampshire, England; 'Middle' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent stone is a precious gemstone.

clue.text: Hits back at box

indicators.note: back says the word for hits is read in reverse

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or hits

explanation.surface: Someone hits back at a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Parrot in city house

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A pet parrot kept in a city home.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district for the City, the financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words back, just as a returning sound does.

clue.text: End product of frightful rips on car

indicators.note: frightful suggests something mangled into an awful mess of letters

explanation.surface: Frightful tears on a vehicle lead to the scrapheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapped metal is what remains when a vehicle reaches the end of its life.

clue.text: Outer garment for one's mammal

parts.note: a coat is worn over other clothes
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An overcoat for someone's pet animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American raccoon-like animal is a mammal.

clue.text: See first at Bath having girth adjusted? It is a plant!

parts.note: to eye something is to see it

indicators.note: first at picks the opening letter of the following word
adjusted says the letters are reset in a new order

explanation.surface: Seeing a horse first at Bath with its girth adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns GIRTH into RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used for eye remedies, a plant.

clue.text: Attack being performed with studio scenery

parts.note: a show that is on is being performed
a set is the scenery for a film or TV studio

explanation.surface: A play being staged with studio scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack, as well as a beginning.
